$comment: Seeded reference data for raw silk grading under IS 15090, BIS specification set.
M1-51 and the M8.5 note in the specification both require that NONE of this appears in
program code. The engine reads this file; it knows no constant of its own.
EVERY row carries "confirmed": false until the Unit In-Charge signs it off against a real
Dharmavaram grading worksheet (OPEN-Q-C13). While anything here is unconfirmed the engine
refuses to compute a grade in live mode — see grade.js. That is the recommended default of
OPEN-Q-C13: 'Do not compute a grade in a live system while any row is still unconfirmed.'
The BIS tables deliberately differ from the ISA tables. They are separate records, not
translations of each other: IS 15090 states that 'the values in respect of maximum deviation
for various grades are different than those specified in International Silk Association
Standards'. Do not derive one from the other.

rounding.$comment: IS 2:1960 — retain the same number of significant places as the specified value.

$comment: OPEN — the divisor is NOT specified by any source read for this project. IS 15090 prints a
worked frequency-distribution example (Fi, di, Fi*di, Fi*di^2) but the sources consulted did
not settle whether the divisor is n or n-1. Seeded as 'n' because the frequency-distribution
presentation of a complete enumeration of specimens reads as a population, but this is a
GUESS and is marked unconfirmed. A real worksheet settles it in one reading: recompute its
printed size deviation both ways and see which matches.
Resolved from the size MARKED OR DECLARED on the bales, never from the measured size.
A lot marked 33 denier may measure 34.5 denier and still pass the 7 per cent gate of WF-74:
the marked size governs category resolution, the measured size governs only the
reading-count rule. See M1-51.
Authoritative Major / Auxiliary classification, per category. This is the store the grade
engine reads. The is_major_characteristic / is_auxiliary_characteristic booleans on
mst_method_parameter are non-authoritative report-ordering defaults ONLY and the engine must
never read them, because they cannot express maximumDeviation being major in Category III
and auxiliary in Categories I and II.

applicability.$comment: Applying cohesion to coarse silk produces a wrong grade that looks plausible, which is why the rule is stated rather than left implicit.

$comment: An auxiliary result below the provisional grade's requirement pulls the grade down, but by
at most one class, and only for the characteristics listed. The cap list is category-scoped:
maximumDeviation is capped only where it is AUXILIARY (I and II). In Category III it is a
major test and the auxiliary cap cannot apply to it.
Ordered best to worst. The engine must support extension without a code change, so the
order is data. 'Lowest grade' means furthest along this list.
NOT SEEDED — deliberately left empty.
The per-grade limit values for each characteristic are the heart of the grading tables and
were NOT available to this project. Inventing them would produce a grade that looks
plausible and is wrong, which is the worst possible failure for a document a buyer settles
money against. The engine therefore REFUSES to grade until this is populated, in draft mode
as well as live mode, and says so by name.
Populate from the unit's own grade tables, one record per category per characteristic:
{ "category": "II", "characteristic": "sizeDeviation", "limits": [
where 'max' is the worst value still allowed for that grade. Use 'min' instead for
characteristics where a higher value is better (neatness, tenacity, cohesion).

repeatRules.$comment: WF-74. Compared against the size MARKED on the bales, not the measured average.

$comment: CONFLICTING SOURCES — do not rely on either figure without a worksheet.
The specification states 4 sizing skeins of 450 m from each of 10 bobbins = 40 readings for
silk up to 3.7 tex, and 8 sizing skeins of 112.5 m from each of 10 bobbins = 80 readings
from 3.8 tex upwards.
The domain research instead records size deviation using 200 skeins x 450 m (fine) or
400 skeins x 112.5 m (coarse), weighed in 10 separate lots.
These are not reconcilable by arithmetic and may reflect BIS versus ISA, or a full grading
versus the local Limited Test. The engine does not care how many readings there are - it
computes over what it is given - but the METHOD MASTER must state the required count, and
M6-03 enforces it. Settle this against a real worksheet before enforcing any count.
From the coarsest and finest specimens, not from the full set. The count depends on
coarseness: 4 and 4 for finer silk, 8 and 8 for coarse.

lowNeatness.$comment: The mean of the worst one-fifth of panels — 4 of 20.

$comment: Oven-dry mass plus the official commercial allowance for silk. The 11 per cent regain is a
constant of trade and is verified; the oven temperature and the convergence thresholds are
standards constants and are also configuration, never code.
